card: Replaces DescriptorScriptPubKeyMan's public RecursiveMutex with a private non-recursive Mutex as part of #19303. External callers across the wallet and RPC code no longer take the lock directly, internal paths are split into lock-held helpers, and address-availability notifications are deferred until after unlocking to avoid re-entrant deadlocks with synchronous callbacks. A regression test is added to exercise callback re-entry and lock release during keypool operations. No changes to RPC output, wallet storage, or keypool semantics are intended.
changed_since_previous: No structural or architectural changes; the commit progression and overall approach remain the same.
evidence: Part of tracking issue #19303 to eliminate recursive mutexes in the codebase (PR description)
Includes a unit test in scriptpubkeyman_tests.cpp covering synchronous callback re-entry during keypool top-ups and address generation (commit 1f29c2b31c)
problem: DescriptorScriptPubKeyMan used a public recursive mutex, allowing external callers to lock internal state directly and obscuring lock order hierarchies across the wallet. Recursive mutexes also prevent full Clang thread-safety annotations and create deadlock hazards when synchronous callbacks query the wallet while the lock is held.

risk.why: Mistakes in wallet mutex refactoring could introduce deadlocks or lock-order inversions that freeze wallet RPCs and UI callbacks.

scope_notes: Commit 2cde6f9534 is a scripted-diff renaming cs_desc_man to m_desc_mutex across the repository.
summary: Replaces DescriptorScriptPubKeyMan's public RecursiveMutex with a private non-recursive Mutex and renames it to m_desc_mutex. Public methods now encapsulate lock acquisition while shared internal logic is split into lock-held helper functions. Address-availability signals are deferred until after the mutex is released to prevent re-entrancy deadlocks during synchronous callbacks.
